thread:
kevin_support: Heads-up — customer (AcmeAnalytics) on Private/VPC deploy seeing intermittent inference failures when streaming. TLS handshake resets after some tokens, reproducible from their side. Can someone triage?

deploy-bot: Escalation created: #TICKET-7892 -> assigned to @kevin_support :white_check_mark:

maria_network: can you paste the SG/NACL configs and any flow logs? also confirm destination port (443?)

kevin_support: yes dst=443. quick error from their side: 
```
2026-03-12T14:03:21Z TLS handshake error: TLSv1.2 alert handshake_failure during post-handshake read
stream terminated after ~12s, client IP x.x.x.x (their NAT EIP)
```

alex_oncall: is this only on long responses/streaming? sounds like ephemeral port or NACL silent-drop. check their ephemeral port range on the hosts: `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`

kevin_support: ran that on one of their inference clients, output: `32768 65535`

sam_engineer: OK. can you also grab the NACL outbound rules for the subnet? NACLs are stateless so an outbound DENY for high ports will drop packets silently. `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids acl-0abcd1234`

kevin_support: pasted relevant part of their NACL outbound rules (redacted):
```
Rule 100: ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 1024-61000
Rule 110: DENY 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 61001-65535
```

maria_network: aha. they allowed up to 61000 but denied 61001-65535 outbound. client ephemeral range goes up to 65535 so clients sometimes pick ports >61000 and NACL drops outbound packets. that would lead to server not receiving full handshake -> resets. :warning:

alex_oncall: exact symptom map: client sends SYN from high-ephemeral (e.g., 62345) -> our server SYN/ACK goes back but outbound NACL blocks reply -> client times out/aborts -> TLS handshake fails mid-stream.

kevin_support: reported to customer, they admitted the NACL was tightened for a compliance change but they missed ephemeral range implications. they applied a patch: changed Rule 100 to `ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 1024-65535` and removed the DENY rule.

kevin_support: after change we saw streaming stable across their test VMs. customer confirms: "streams are no longer failing" :tada:

sam_engineer: adding quick KB snippet to ticket: 
- verify host ephemeral range: `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`
- check NACL outbound allow ranges include ephemeral ports (recommended 49152-65535 or up to host-configured max)
- aws cli examples: `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0abc123` and `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abcd1234 --rule-number 100 --protocol tcp --rule-action allow --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress`

maria_network: also tcpdump quick repro filter if needed: `tcpdump -n -i eth0 host x.x.x.x and port 443 and tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-ack) != 0`

alex_oncall: closing notes: this one was a "silent outbound deny" caused by NACL rule ordering/coverage. KB: check both SGs (stateful) and NACLs (stateless) — NACL denies are common root cause for silent streaming failures.

kevin_support: marking #TICKET-7892 resolved with root cause: NACL outbound range denied ephemeral ports. customer updated NACL, validated. thanks all.
